name: Teal 'tail' livery (2000s)
description: WestJet's scheme before 2018, still on some 737-700s: a white fuselage with 'WEST' in navy and 'JET' in teal, heavy slanted capitals over the forward windows, followed by a small teal-and-navy flag of the tail; a teal fin with a white chevron pointing aft from the trailing edge, navy in the chevron's fork down to the root and along the dorsal fin, teal again behind it; a thin white line up the leading edge. White engines; winglets teal over navy.

sources.title: C-FGWJ (32854076854).jpg (CC BY-SA 2.0)
sources.note: C-FGWJ (737-700) right side on the ground, square on, in sun, 2017-02-11: flipped and fitted to the measured 737-700 shape (tools/photo_trace.py, doors pinned); the fin's navy and white chevron traced by color, the title and its mark. The winglet's outer face shows too: teal over navy with a white band between.

sources.title: C-FGWJ YVR (18225545532).jpg (CC BY-SA 2.0)
sources.note: C-FGWJ left side climbing, 2015-04-17: the fin's design faces forward on the left too (mirrored); the navy reads blue against the sky.

sources.title: C-FGWJ on Planespotters.net (evidence only, not openly licensed)
sources.note: Right side, recent (2025): still in this scheme; winglets teal over navy with a white band.

teal.name: WestJet's older teal (#03547A-#105468 in sun and sky light, #007395 on the 2025 photo): deeper than the 2018 teal

navy.name: navy: a dark blue that still reads blue in sun (#07174D in shade, #233053 against the sky, #002159 on the 2025 photo), not black

areas.name: thin white line up the leading edge, above the chevron
white chevron: its upper arm from the leading edge rising to a point at the trailing edge, its lower arm from there down to the root
navy in the chevron's fork, down to the root (the dorsal fin ahead of it navy too)

logos.description: The tail in miniature, as a little flag after 'WESTJET' (forward of it on the right).
The same after the title on the left (aft of it).

titles.style: Heavy slanted capitals, 'WEST' navy and 'JET' teal, the J dropping below the line; over the forward windows, a little above them.

notes: Measured on C-FGWJ's right side (flipped); the left side's fin matches mirrored (2015 photo). On the right the title reads 'WESTJET' then the flag, forward; the left is taken as the mirror, the flag aft of the title (its place not measured: medium). The fit to the 737-700 left the title's height above the windows uncertain by about 0.1 m. The Canadian flag and 'Proudly Canadian' over the aft windows aren't drawn.
history: WestJet's scheme through the 2000s and 2010s, replaced from 2018 by the current one; some 737-700s still wear it in 2025.
